column8: Actions / Recommendation

The Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for LPG and SLG were not available at the facility. SDS must be properly displayed at prominent locations and in the local language (Urdu) to ensure accessibility and understanding. It is essential to implement, maintain, and regularly update the SDS for regulatory compliance and workplace safety. Additionally, training on both SDSs should be conducted for all relevant staff, and documentary evidence of these trainings must be maintained for verification and audit purposes.

Routine inspections of LPG and SNG tanks are carried out regularly by both the Powerhouse and HSE teams. However, these inspections are not documented. It is essential to maintain proper inspection records to ensure regulatory compliance and traceability.

No controlled Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are available for LPG transfer, storage, and emergency shutdown. It is essential to ensure the availability of controlled SOPs through the IMS system and to display them in the local language at the LPG facility for effective communication and compliance.
The mechanical integrity is conducted. However, a formal plan needs to be developed, documented, and periodically reviewed to ensure compliance with safety standards.

Process Safety Management (PSM) is currently not implemented at the CBL site, and no training on PSM has been provided to employees involved in the operation and maintenance of the LPG system. Additionally, operational SOP training for LPG storage has not been conducted for the relevant staff.
There is a need to establish a comprehensive operations and maintenance SOP training plan for all concerned personnel.
Leak detection system, and pressure gauges are installed, working, and calibrated. However, LEL detectors have not been calibrated and requir immediate attention to ensure reliable gas monitoring.

Workers involved in LPG loading and unloading are experienced; however, no documented training records are available. It is essential to conduct formal, documented training followed by written validation to ensure proper understanding of loading/unloading procedures and safe LPG handling practices.
Emergency shut-off valves are operational and have been tested. However, they should also be tested during emergency mock drills to evaluate response time and effectiveness in real-time scenarios.

Hose assemblies are pressure-rated and have undergone pressure testing. However, to ensure full compliance, all hoses must remain within their inspection validity period, and test records should be consistently maintained. Inspection and testing should be carried out as part of preventive maintenance (PM) planning on annual basis.
These all found leak-free but show some signs of corrosion. It is recommended to inspect and replace any corroded components to ensure long-term safety and functionality.

Emergency drills have not been conducted or documented on an annual basis. It is essential to develop and implement regular emergency response drills covering various LPG storage scenarios, and to maintain proper documentation to ensure preparedness and compliance with safety standards.

A Zone Classification study has not yet been conducted for the LPG storage facility. It is necessary to arrange an Area/Zone Classification assessment through a qualified third-party expert to ensure compliance with safety standards and proper hazardous area identification.
Fireproofing of the structural supports and vessel skirts of the LPG storage is strongly recommended and is required as per applicable standards.

No lightning arrestors were found installed on the LPG storage tanks, posing a serious risk of ignition in the event of a lightning strike. It is strongly recommended to install certified lightning protection systems, properly connected to an effective earthing network, preferably at the nearest elevated structure, such as the FG warehouse.

There is no shed installed over the LPG decanting pump, leaving it exposed to direct sunlight, rain, and dust. It is recommended to install a properly designed non-combustible shed to protect the pump from environmental elements, prevent equipment degradation, and reduce potential fire or operational hazards in line with good engineering and safety practices.

Tagging and color coding are properly done on pipelines, but identification tags are missing on vessels, such as those for SNG, Air, and vapor vessel. It is recommended to affix clear and durable tags on all vessels to ensure proper identification and enhance operational and emergency response safety in line with industry standards.

No cabinet was found at the entrance of the LPG storage area for placing mobile phones or other electronic devices. It is recommended to install a dedicated cabinet at the entry point to restrict the entry of potential ignition sources and ensure compliance with hazardous area safety protocols.

No PPE cabinet or mandatory personal protective equipmen (PPE) such as helmets, FR suit, anti-static shoes, goggles, or gloves were available at the LPG area. Additionally, PPE complaince is not being followed by personnel. It is strongly recommended to provide a well-stocked PPE cabinet at the entry point and ensure strick enforcement of PPE usage within the LPG storage area for personnel safety and regulatory compliance.

Inaccessible Fire Hydrants in LPG Area:
Fire hydrants in the LPG storage area were found obstructed, making them difficult to access during an emergency. Blocked access can significantly delay emergency response and compromise fire control efforts.  There is need to ensure all fire equipments are eassily accessible, unobstructed, and clearly marked with visible signage. maintain a 1- meter clearance zone around each hydrant at all times in accordance with fire safety standards (e.g. NFPA-25).

Absence Of External Fire Brigade Inlet valve:
No external fire brigade connection (inlet valve) was found on the firefighting pipeline in the LPG area. this valve is essential for allowing external fire tenders to pump water into the internal fire hydrant system during a major fire.

Remove the wire rope from the area to eliminate the potential hazard.

ESD team implemented SAP-based repair & maintenance plan (completed). Regular Sunday maintenance ongoing. Corrective and preventive actions embedded in SAP.

To overcome short circuiting, HSE team initiated a mini electrical safety project. Plant-wide survey completed, report finalized and reviewed, with an action plan developed. Execution is planned from Q1 to Q4 2026, budget allocated.

There are 11 ovens in total, with Line-1 to Line-5 not having a manual windout system. As a first backup and first safety, UPS systems are installed across all lines. HSE team evaluated Line-1 oven for a manual windout, engaging FEECOM team to design and install it. The system worked but did not generate the required torque, making it ineffective. The installation has now been returned to FEECOM for redesign and reinstallation.

HSE team conducts frequent SOAP test audits with ESD team to monitor gas leaks. In the recent audit, 23 leakage points were identified; 20 rectified, remaining points to be addressed through ongoing maintenance. Gas leak issues are monitored and rectified time to time to ensure safety.

SOP compliance has been reinforced across all departments. Permit to Work (PTW) compliance is ensured, with PTWs obtained before every activity. Consequence management has been finalized, and violators are addressed according to the defined consequence management metrics.

In Line-1 oven, manual ignition is required to create the fire triangle, which previously led to an explosion incident. Safety systems of Line-1 and Line-2 ovens are compromised, with weak integrity and high gas consumption. HSE conducted detailed inspection and proposed replacement of both ovens. Budget approved, replacement planned by end 2026 or early 2027.

A plant-wide survey will be conducted to identify all wet and slippery floor areas, especially in high-risk locations such as washing and chemical handling areas. Based on findings, anti-slip mats and anti-slip flooring solutions will be installed in coordination with the Project & Admin Department.

A short inspection will be conducted to identify all unfixed or loose MS sheets on floors and walkways. All identified sheets will be properly secured using appropriate fasteners to prevent tripping hazards.
Housekeeping practices will be strengthened across the plant to ensure proper placement of tools, materials, and equipment in designated areas, keeping walkways clear and safe.
Spill response procedures will be reinforced, with strategically placed spill kits and trained chemical handlers ensuring immediate cleanup to prevent slip hazards.
Temporary floor tapes will be replaced with durable industrial floor markings to prevent peeling and tripping hazards.
1346 steps of stairs inspected across all plant; ~300 identified as slippery. Staircase nosing pads demand raised; installation after receipt.

A formal Machine Safety Bypass Protocol will be developed. Any bypassing of machine safety systems will only be allowed through approved procedures, risk assessment, and authorization. Unauthorized bypassing will strictly be prohibited and shall be addressed in accordance with the Consequence Management SOP.
Behavioral safety awareness are being reinforced through BBS program sessions and toolbox talks focusing on safe work pace and hazard awareness.
Machine safety sessions will emphasize keeping hands clear of moving parts and proper use of guarding.
Supervisory monitoring will be strengthened and employees will be reminded to strictly follow SOPs and safety instructions, with non-compliance addressed through the consequence management system.
Unsafe crossing behaviors will be corrected through installation of crossovers and safety awareness sessions.

A detailed survey of the packing sections has been conducted to identify locations where crossovers are required. Based on this assessment, a budget of 9 million has been allocated in CAPEX 2026 for the procurement of stainless steel crossovers. The next steps involve engaging a third-party vendor to take precise on-site measurements, followed by fabrication of the crossovers. Once fabricated, the crossovers will be installed to ensure safe movement within the packing sections.
Workstations will be assessed to identify areas requiring stainless steel benches. Procurement and installation will follow the assessment for ergonomic and safe working conditions.
Materials and tools will be stored in designated locations to maintain clear walking paths.
Installation of crossovers will eliminate unsafe crossing. Any future violations post-installation will be treated as unsafe behavior and addressed via the consequence management system.
Similar corrective actions as conveyor crossings will apply. Unsafe crossings will be prohibited after crossovers are installed, with violations handled through consequence management.

A plant-wide, department-wise, and activity-wise assessment of mandatory PPE requirements has been conducted and the final report need to be issued. Overall PPE compliance currently stands at 21%. All stakeholders are required to procure all mandatory PPEs and ensure full compliance across their respective areas.
Compliance with safety footwear will be enforced across departments.
Non-slip shoes will be ensured for employees in wet or slippery areas.
Mandatory use of safety goggles for dust, chemical, or particle exposure will be reinforced.
Included in HSE Mini Safety Projects. 437 machines surveyed; 1053 safeties identified (697 intact, 356 faulty). Report finalized with action plan. Execution started from Q1 2026 to Q-3 2026

Regular safety trainings are ongoing. One Point Lessons (OPLs) have been developed and shared for recordable incidents. About 1300 workers have been covered through on-site safety sessions so far, remaining workers will be covered on regular safety sessions on site.
Part of HSE Mini Projects. 1329 guards identified (1001 intact, 328 missing, 160 proposed). Action plan finalized; execution from Q1 2026 to Q-3 2026
Part Of HSE Mini Projects. Plant-wide survey completed covering activities, access and platforms. Execution planned from Q1–Q4 2026.
Manual handling trainings will continue across departments. All manual handling equipment, including pallet jacks and trolleys, will be inspected and repaired to ensure safe handling operations.

All task-specific and machine-specific SOPs need to be reviewed and updated based on injury analysis. Emphasis should be placed on real-time reinforcement of SOPs and continuous compliance monitoring on the shop floor to ensure safe operations.

LOTO implementation scope has been defined, BOQ prepared, and budget allocated. CAR Needs to be raised, after CAR Approval, Precourement will start,  followed by installation and formal implementation of the LOTO system.

All workers whose jobs involve chemical handling will be trained on safe chemical handling procedures. Job-specific chemical gloves and other mandatory PPE must be procured and provided by the respective department or stakeholders responsible for these workers. Departments must ensure continuous compliance with PPE usage at all times during chemical handling tasks.
Heat stress awareness sessions conducted. Hydration, rest breaks and monitoring of high-temperature areas ensured.

All equipment with potential sharp edges that may come into contact with workers must be regularly inspected through daily safety observations. A consolidated report of all identified sharp edges should be prepared. Based on this report, corrective actions must be planned and executed during maintenance or shutdowns to ensure all equipment is made safe for worker interaction
Equipment failures rectified. Preventive and breakdown maintenance strengthened by ESD team.
All tools across the plant will be inspected to identify improper or unsafe tools. Necessary corrections or replacements will be implemented to ensure safe tool usage at all workstations.

Currently, lifting activities at CBL are handled by an uncertified rigging team. HSE has finalized a maintenance contract with a certified rigging contractor; the agreement is under legal submission. Work will commence upon legal approval.

The CBL lux level audit report shall be compared against the EBM lux level standards. Any gaps identified through this comparison must be addressed through appropriate corrective actions to ensure compliance with the required illumination levels
All storage areas will require mandatory helmet use, and safety awareness will be reinforced for personnel working in stacking and storage zones. Inspections will monitor compliance.

A safe driving training session will be conducted in collaboration with NHA for management, lower management, and plant vehicle operators. Follow-up inspections will ensure adoption of safe driving practices across the plant.
